stem.text: A beam of red laser light of wavelength $633\,\text{nm}$ is incident normally on a diffraction grating with $600$ lines per $\text{mm}$.

stem.alt: Light beam travelling right into a diffraction grating, with three rays drawn to a vertical screen, labelled first-order maximum above, zero-order maximum in the centre and first-order maximum below, and the label screen.

stem.text: The beam of red light is now replaced by a beam of blue laser light of wavelength $445\,\text{nm}$. A replacement diffraction grating is used so that the first-order maximum of the blue light appears at the same position on the screen as the first-order maximum of the red light from the original laser.
How many lines per mm are there in the replacement diffraction grating?
